title: Two inverse-image stalk elements have unit representatives on one open
statement: Let $f:Z\to X$ be a continuous map of topological spaces, and let $A$ be a sheaf of sets on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. The sets may lie in any universe at least as large as the space universe. Write $L=f^{-1}A$ for the constructed sheaf inverse image and $\eta:A\to f_*L$ for its adjunction unit. For any $z\in Z$ and any $s,t\in L_z$, where $L_z$ is the colimit of sections over open neighbourhoods of $z$ [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-stalk], there exist an open $W\ni f(z)$ and $a,b\in A(W)$ with $(\eta_W(a))_z=s$ and $(\eta_W(b))_z=t$.

proof.text: Represent each element by a section on a neighbourhood N, using joint surjectivity of the neighbourhood-colimit coprojections.

For the presheaf left Kan extension P, let theta be its sheafification unit and let R be the locally generated image of theta. R is a subsheaf of the sheafification. The sheafification universal property extends the map from P to R to a map l from its sheafification to R. The composite of l and the inclusion of R is the identity: both agree on theta, and sheafification hom-ext cancels theta. Hence every section is locally in the image of theta. For the section on N, choose a smaller neighbourhood V of z and a preimage in P(V).

source.place: Tag 00WK, local surjectivity of the sheafification unit; the subsheaf-image argument follows the universal property

proof.text: The pointwise left Kan extension is a colimit over open W with V contained in f^{-1}W. Joint surjectivity of its coprojections gives a section on some W. W contains f(z), since V contains z. The constructed unit is the Kan-extension unit followed by theta. Naturality of theta and the stalk-colimit relations identify its unit germ with the original element.
Perform this for s and t. Restrict the two sections to W1 intersect W2. Naturality of the unit and the colimit relations preserve both germs.

theorem inverse_image_stalk_pair_representatives
    {X Z : TopCat.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ X) (A : X.Sheaf (Type (max u w))) (z : Z)
    (s t : colimit ((OpenNhds.inclusion z).op ⋙
      ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback
        (Opens.map f) (Type (max u w))
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (Opens.grothendieckTopology Z)).obj A).obj)) :
    ∃ (W : Opens X) (hzW : f z ∈ W) (a b : A.obj.obj (op W)),
      colimit.ι ((OpenNhds.inclusion z).op ⋙
        ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback
          (Opens.map f) (Type (max u w))
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (Opens.grothendieckTopology Z)).obj A).obj)
        (op ⟨(Opens.map f).obj W, hzW⟩)
        (((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
          (Opens.map f) (Type (max u w))
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (Opens.grothendieckTopology Z)).unit.app A).hom.app
            (op W) a) = s ∧
      colimit.ι ((OpenNhds.inclusion z).op ⋙
        ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback
          (Opens.map f) (Type (max u w))
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (Opens.grothendieckTopology Z)).obj A).obj)
        (op ⟨(Opens.map f).obj W, hzW⟩)
        (((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
          (Opens.map f) (Type (max u w))
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (Opens.grothendieckTopology Z)).unit.app A).hom.app
            (op W) b) = t
